evidence_profile.biological_context: Openly consented samples from people who declared themselves healthy, grouped by population label. The callsets describe germline variation in reference cohorts; no tissue, expression or phenotype data accompany the variants.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Observational genotype calls with sample and population metadata. No effect size or per-variant uncertainty is attached, and call quality differs between SNV, indel and SV callsets.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: None for mechanism. Presence of an allele in a healthy-declared cohort is indirect evidence of tolerance only and cannot separate a benign allele from one with recessive, late-onset or reduced-penetrance effects.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Observation in healthy-declared individuals argues against a high-penetrance, early-onset dominant effect of that allele; it does not exclude recessive, late-onset or reduced-penetrance effects.
evidence_profile.absence_means: An allele missing from the callset was not observed in this cohort. Coverage, callset design and population representation decide what could be seen; absence is not evidence of rarity or harm.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Single-chain structure models of UniProt reference sequences. Ligands, binding partners, membranes, modifications and alternative conformations are not modelled.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Computational model. Per-residue confidence (pLDDT) is the only uncertainty provided and measures confidence of the model, not experimental support.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low on its own. A model can place a residue in a buried, exposed or interface-like environment; it cannot show that a substitution changes stability, binding or activity.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None. Supports reasoning about missense and in-frame changes only in combination with experimental structures, domain annotation and variant-level assays.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A protein or isoform without a model, or a low-confidence region, has no usable structural context here; this is not evidence of disorder or of the lack of a structure.

The class thresholds (0.34 and 0.564) were chosen for 90% precision on pathogenic and benign ClinVar variants, so ClinVar-based benchmarks of the classes are not independent of the calibration; the Ensembl VEP plugin page states that the model was not trained on ClinVar variants. The paper describing training and calibration was not readable here (bot challenge)
Missense only

Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike), so the data stay in the git-ignored data/ area.

status.notes: GCS bucket metadata and MD5 verified.

unverified_fields: training and calibration details (paper not retrievable)
which licence statement governs the 2023 data files

evidence_profile.biological_context: Predicts a pathogenicity class for single amino-acid substitutions per transcript or isoform. No tissue, cell-type, dosage, inheritance or mechanism context is carried.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Computational prediction. Class thresholds were chosen to reach 90% precision on ClinVar labels although the model was not trained on ClinVar variants, so agreement with ClinVar is calibration and not independent confirmation. No per-variant uncertainty is provided.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low. The score does not say whether a change causes loss or gain of function, destabilisation or a dominant-negative effect, and it cannot see effects that act through splicing or regulation.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: A pathogenicity likelihood for the substitution; no phenotype, penetrance or mode of inheritance.
evidence_profile.absence_means: No score exists for synonymous, nonsense, splice, indel, structural or non-coding variants. Absence of a prediction is not evidence of a benign effect.

sources.scope: Haploinsufficiency and triplosensitivity scores for genes and genomic regions, recurrent CNV regions (V2.1), and curated gene-disease validity.
identifiers: HGNC symbol and NCBI Gene ID
sources.mapping_methods: Gene- and region-level; coordinates given for GRCh37 and GRCh38.

licence.redistribution: Open; keep attribution

evidence_profile.biological_context: Expert-panel curation of whole genes and genomic regions: dosage sensitivity (loss or gain of an entire gene or region), recurrent CNV regions and gene-disease validity. Gene- and region-level assertions; recurrent regions are intervals.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Graded by curators from published cases. Dosage scores encode evidence levels; 30 stands for a gene associated with an autosomal recessive phenotype and 40 for dosage sensitivity unlikely. A curated judgement, not a measurement, and not allele-specific.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate for the dosage mechanism of whole-gene or whole-region loss or gain. It says nothing about the mechanism of a particular small variant, and contiguous-gene or position effects of multi-gene CNVs are not separated.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Curated association of dosage change (and, in the validity records, of gene disruption) with a named phenotype; penetrance and expressivity vary.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A gene or region without a record has not been curated, which differs from a score meaning no evidence (0) or dosage sensitivity unlikely (40). Absence is not evidence of dosage tolerance.

version.value: VCF fileDate 2026-10-19

sources.mapping_methods: Submitters provide HGVS; NCBI normalises and maps to GRCh37/GRCh38.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Submitter-asserted interpretations of variants for named conditions. Each submission carries its own review status, classification, condition and evidence summary; germline and other classifications are separate fields.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Aggregate classification with review status and conflicting-interpretation flags. These grade the assertion, not the underlying evidence; submissions often rest on the same upstream evidence, so agreement between submitters is not independent confirmation.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: None as structured data. A classification asserts clinical significance and does not establish mechanism; any functional evidence is in free text.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Condition-specific clinical significance (pathogenic to benign, or uncertain significance) as named by the submitter.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant missing from ClinVar has not been submitted, which reflects ascertainment (tested genes, populations, laboratories) and not benignity. Uncertain significance means unresolved, not benign.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Biochemical assays (chromatin accessibility, transcription-factor binding, histone modification, RNA expression) in biosamples, and candidate cis-regulatory elements derived from them. Activity is specific to the biosample.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Direct measurements of biochemical activity of regions in a biosample. Candidate element classes are computed from those assays and are annotations, not demonstrations of regulatory function.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate for the statement that a region is biochemically active in a biosample. No allele-specific effect, target gene or direction of effect is given, and activity does not prove that the element is required for regulation.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None directly; places variants in regions that are candidates for regulatory effects in particular cell types.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant outside every annotated element may still act in untested cell types, states or at long range. Absence of a peak reflects the assayed biosamples and thresholds.

sources.scope: Reference assemblies and annotation. 563 human genome records in the selector: GRCh38.p14 (reference, GENCODE annotation), GRCh37.p13, T2T-CHM13v2.0 and 560 haplotype assemblies. The GRCh38 reference sequence (toplevel FASTA) and the release-116 gene annotation (GTF) are mirrored.
formats: FASTA (bgzip with .fai and .gzi) and GTF, downloaded for GRCh38 release 116
sources.mapping_methods: Stable Ensembl IDs with cross-references; liftover/assembly mapping through Ensembl tools.

quantitative.summary: Not applicable (reference data).

licence.name: Ensembl imposes no restrictions on access to or use of the data (disclaimer page)
licence.redistribution: Unrestricted per the disclaimer; check third-party components

sources.update_frequency: Integrated releases several times a year (2026-07 live).
coverage_limitations: GRCh38 only: the GRCh37, T2T-CHM13 and haplotype assemblies have registry records but no sequence or annotation files here
The FASTA is the unmasked toplevel set (706 sequences, including patches and haplotypes); no soft-masked or primary-assembly-only file is held
The GTF is the default release-116 file; the larger chr_patch_hapl_scaff file (patch and haplotype annotation) and the ab initio predictions are not held
Release 116 postdates the MANE v1.5 and AlphaMissense transcript sets: transcript versions can differ, so joins on transcript IDs must compare versions
known_omissions: Variation and regulation data exist for few of the 560 sample assemblies (96 with variation, 2 with regulation)

reuse_decision.rationale: The GRCh38 toplevel FASTA (808 MB) and the release-116 GTF (141 MB) are the reference every coordinate file in the library is checked against, publish checksums, and have no curated alternative inside the library. They are fetched and verified against the Ensembl CHECKSUMS. For human the Ensembl README states that the GTF equals the GENCODE gene set, so GENCODE's own copy is not fetched. The genome registry (existing asset) is kept as is. The remote range reads of the same FASTA stay as an independent route and are tested against the local copy.

status.notes: REST and FTP reachable. The web docs for VEP plugins returned HTTP 504 at probe time. The FASTA and GTF downloads equal the BSD checksums and sizes published in the Ensembl CHECKSUMS files; the indexed FASTA is also readable over HTTPS by region (index opens in about 5 s, a region read takes about 1 s).

mechanism_evidence.note: exon and intron structure of transcript models
reading frame and exon junctions needed to evaluate decay

evidence_profile.biological_context: Reference assemblies (primary, alternate and patch sequences, T2T-CHM13 and haplotype assemblies) and gene annotation. The GRCh38 reference is a single consensus sequence and its annotation is a set of transcript models, not a map of which isoform is expressed where.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Reference data. The properties to verify are coordinates and sequence (done here by published checksums and reference-allele concordance), not an effect or association strength.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Not applicable. It supplies the sequence and transcript frame needed to define consequences (exon boundaries, reading frame, splice sites) and asserts no effect.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None: reference sequence and gene models carry no phenotype information.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A position outside annotated genes is not shown to be non-functional. Sequence that is carried only on alternate or haplotype assemblies may be unmappable on the primary reference.

overlaps_with_sources.note: the human gene annotation distributed by Ensembl is merged with the GENCODE gene set

quantitative.summary: Plugin data carry their source scores (e.g. MaveDB scores, SpliceAI delta scores, LOEUF).

licence.name: Ensembl: no restrictions on data (verified); plugin resources carry upstream terms (e.g. gnomAD notes SpliceAI annotations as CC BY-NC 4.0)
licence.redistribution: Check each plugin resource before redistribution

sources.update_frequency: With each Ensembl release; plugin files updated irregularly (MaveDB file dated 2026-03-09).
coverage_limitations: Plugin data licences are those of the underlying resources. The plugin page states some of them (dbNSFP has separate academic and commercial branches; PromoterAI needs a licence agreement; the AlphaMissense text conflicts with the licence in the data file we hold) and is silent on others
SpliceAI, Enformer, mutfunc, ProtVar and SpliceVault files are large (see the listing evidence); Ensembl does not generate SpliceAI scores for indels
known_omissions: Only the MaveDB plugin file is acquired; the other plugin data are catalogued with their sizes and not fetched
The plugin list was read from the documentation page; the plugins' own code and the data files' internal formats were not inspected

status.notes: FTP listings and the plugin documentation page are reachable (the page returned HTTP 504 in an earlier probe and was read on retry). MaveDB CHECKSUMS file lists BSD sum 22727 / 547461 KiB.

unverified_fields: per-plugin data licences not stated on the plugin page

mechanism_evidence.note: rule-based consequence terms (for example frameshift, stop gained) against transcript models

components.name: predictor plugins (for example SpliceAI, SpliceVault, Enformer, AlphaMissense)

evidence_profile.biological_context: A tool that annotates variants against transcript models and attaches plugin data. Every annotation is computed or looked up per transcript, so one variant can carry different consequences across transcripts and tools.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Mixed, and inherited from the plugin: consequence terms are deterministic rules against annotation, predictor plugins are hypotheses, MaveDB values are measurements and LOEUF is a gene-level population estimate. The evidence kind of each part persists.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate depending on the plugin. A consequence term names a molecular consequence class and does not show loss versus gain of function or tissue context; agreement between predictor plugins is not independent confirmation because they can share training data.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None directly.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A missing plugin value means that plugin has no data for the variant (type, transcript or build); for example precomputed SpliceAI files cover SNVs in MANE Select transcripts and no indels. Absence is not a negative prediction.

sources.name: eQTL Catalogue

version.value: Release 7 and pre-release r8_beta (FTP directory dated 2026-01-28); home page cites 32 published studies

sources.scope: Uniformly processed gene-expression and splicing QTL summary statistics and SuSiE fine-mapped credible sets from public human studies.
sources.mapping_methods: Uniform pipeline on GRCh38.

quantitative.summary: Beta, SE, p-value, PIP and credible-set membership.
quantitative.units: SD of normalised expression per allele

licence.name: Data under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International; code under Apache 2.0 (eQTL Catalogue License page)
licence.redistribution: Attribution required; cite Kerimov et al. 2021 (Nat Genet 53:1290) and Kerimov et al. 2023 (PLoS Genet 19:e1010932)

coverage_limitations: REST API v2 and v3 endpoints return HTTP 410 (retired); access is via FTP only
Per-study sample sizes vary widely
known_omissions: Metadata tables are hosted in a GitHub repository outside this session scope

reuse_decision.rationale: Open Targets already consumes eQTL Catalogue credible sets for colocalisation; defer direct download of the very large sumstats until a locus-level analysis requires them.

status.notes: FTP listing verified; API retired.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Public human studies, each with its own tissue or cell type, condition, quantification method and sample size, processed uniformly. Effects are changes in an expression or splicing phenotype per alternate allele in that context.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Statistical association with summary statistics and SuSiE fine-mapped credible sets. Credible sets narrow the candidate variants but do not establish the causal variant.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate for the regulatory axis. A QTL says a variant, or a linked variant, is associated with expression or splicing of a gene in that context; colocalisation with a trait and functional assays are needed to connect it to a phenotype.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: A molecular phenotype (gene expression or splice-event usage) in the studied tissue or cell type; not a disease phenotype.
evidence_profile.absence_means: No QTL means no association was detected in the sampled contexts at the available power. Tissues, cell states, developmental stages and rare alleles that were not sampled are unaddressed.

sources.name: GENCODE and MANE transcript sets

version.value: GENCODE v50 (files dated 2026-06-09); MANE v1.5 (2025-12-04)

sources.scope: Comprehensive human gene annotation (GENCODE) and the matched Ensembl/RefSeq clinical transcript set (MANE Select / Plus Clinical).
sources.mapping_methods: Matched Ensembl and RefSeq transcripts at identical genomic positions.

quantitative.summary: Not applicable.

licence.name: GENCODE: 'all the GENCODE project data is open access' (GENCODE data-access page), under the EMBL-EBI Terms of Use (freely available, no additional restriction, attribution expected). MANE files are hosted by NCBI: NCBI places no restrictions on use or distribution, though original submitters may claim rights, and acknowledgement of NLM is requested.
licence.redistribution: Open with attribution (cite GENCODE and MANE); NCBI notes that third-party rights may exist in submitted data. Only the MANE files are acquired here.

coverage_limitations: MANE covers one transcript per protein-coding gene
GENCODE's own annotation files are not held; the Ensembl release-116 GTF is held instead

reuse_decision.rationale: MANE files are small and fix the transcript choice needed to interpret HGVS across ClinVar, MaveDB and gnomAD. GENCODE's own annotation and FASTA are not fetched: for human the Ensembl README states that the Ensembl GTF equals the GENCODE gene set, and the release-116 GTF and FASTA are held through the ensembl_genomes source (its genebuild was last updated 2025-11 and may differ from GENCODE v50, dated 2026-06-09).

status.notes: Directory listings verified.

mechanism_evidence.note: transcript structure on which decay rules are evaluated
the transcript that defines protein-level variant nomenclature

evidence_profile.biological_context: Transcript models. The GENCODE comprehensive set lists supported transcripts; MANE Select designates one matched Ensembl and RefSeq transcript per gene as a clinical reference, and MANE Plus Clinical adds transcripts required to report variants.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Curated and automated annotation of transcript structure. Choosing a MANE transcript is a convention and not evidence of the dominant isoform in any tissue.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Not applicable. It defines the frame (exons, coding sequence, start and stop) in which consequences are computed, and the consequence depends on the transcript chosen.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None directly. A consequence in a non-MANE isoform can be misread as benign or damaging, so consequences are reported per transcript.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A gene without a MANE Select transcript, or a variant outside MANE transcripts, has no clinical-reference consequence here; this reflects the transcript set and not benignity.

sources.name: gnomAD constraint metrics (LoF/missense) and pext

version.value: v4.1.2 constraint metrics (TSV.bgz 574.5 MB, 2026-09-23); v4.1 file of 2024-04-18 superseded

sources.scope: Gene and transcript constraint (observed/expected LoF, missense, synonymous; LOEUF), mutation and methylation rate tables, base-level pext.
sources.mapping_methods: Gene/transcript level; join on Ensembl IDs.

quantitative.summary: o/e ratios with confidence bounds, Z scores, LOEUF.

licence.name: CC0 for primary data (policies page)
licence.redistribution: Open

sources.update_frequency: Per gnomAD release; 4.1.2 updated constraint only.
coverage_limitations: Constraint is a population-genetic inference, not a direct knockout phenotype
Short genes have wide confidence intervals
The LoF curation held is one small file (734 variants in genes with incomplete penetrance); the v2.1.1 curation sets are not in the public buckets
known_omissions: Ensembl also ships a LOEUF plugin file (338 MB); this is the primary source

reuse_decision.rationale: Primary source of record and moderate size; the Ensembl LOEUF file is a derivative of the same resource so is not downloaded separately.

status.notes: S3 object size verified by HEAD.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Gene- and transcript-level observed/expected counts of predicted loss-of-function, missense and synonymous variants in the gnomAD cohorts. Reflects selection against heterozygous variants, not against recessive-only effects.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Statistical depletion estimates with confidence bounds. They depend on the expectation model (mutation and methylation rates), coverage and sample size, and are weak for small genes.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low for any individual variant. Constraint is a gene property and does not say that a specific allele is damaging; strong constraint supports haploinsufficiency or severe missense sensitivity as a hypothesis.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Intolerance to loss of function suggests, but does not show, a severe early-onset dominant phenotype. Tolerance does not exclude recessive disease, gain of function or missense mechanisms.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A gene without metrics (too few expected variants or poor coverage) is unscored, not unconstrained. A tolerant score is not evidence that a particular allele is benign.

overlaps_with_sources.note: constraint is computed from the gnomAD callsets; the counts are the same observations

sources.name: gnomAD structural variants and copy-number variants

version.value: SVs v4.1.0, CNVs v4.1.0 (site header); also SVs v2.1

sources.scope: Genome SV callset (sites VCF, 1.74 GB, 2,154,486 records: 1,206,278 DEL, 356,035 BND, 304,645 INS, 269,326 DUP, 15,189 CPX, 2,193 INV, 721 multi-allelic CNV, 99 CTX; all with SVTYPE and END) and exome CNV callset (8.9 MB VCF; non-neuro and non-neuro-controls subsets). Both are GRCh38.
sources.mapping_methods: Interval-based on GRCh38.

quantitative.summary: Allele counts and frequencies per ancestry group and SV type; multi-allelic CNV sites (SVTYPE=CNV, 721 records) carry copy-number counts and frequencies (CN_COUNT, CN_FREQ, CN_NUMBER) instead of a single AF.
quantitative.units: counts / frequency in [0, 1]; SVLEN in bp

licence.name: CC0 for primary data (policies page)
licence.redistribution: Open

coverage_limitations: CNV callset is exome-based so non-coding CNVs are missed
For interval overlap only DEL, DUP, INV, CPX, CNV and MCNV records with END > POS are treated as intervals; INS, BND and CTX are points or breakends
Short-read SV sensitivity is limited for repeats and complex events
known_omissions: Long-read SV catalogue (release/lr) was listed but not inspected

reuse_decision.rationale: Both VCFs are fetched and validated: the exome CNV VCF (8.9 MB) and the genome SV sites VCF (1.74 GB; size from the S3 listing, MD5 from the downloads page). They complement the older control-cohort DGV catalogue and the ClinGen dosage regions.

status.notes: S3 listings give exact sizes; both files downloaded, checksum-verified and validated.

mechanism_evidence.note: PREDICTED_LOF, PREDICTED_COPY_GAIN and related gene-overlap annotations

evidence_profile.biological_context: Germline SV calls (genome callset) and CNV calls (exome callset) in the gnomAD cohorts. Algorithm and evidence fields record how each call was made, and PREDICTED_* INFO fields annotate the gene-level consequence of each call.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Population allele counts and frequencies for calls made by combining several algorithms. Sensitivity differs by size and type, and PREDICTED_* consequences are annotation predictions and not assays.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate. Dosage-type consequences (whole-gene deletion, duplication, exon overlap) follow from gene overlap; effects of breakpoints on regulation, gene fusion and position effects are not assessed.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Frequency in population controls bounds pathogenic claims for dosage-sensitive genes; it does not give a phenotype.
evidence_profile.absence_means: Absence from the callset reflects detectability (size, type, repeat context, coverage) as well as rarity; poorly mappable regions are under-called.

sources.name: gnomAD v4.1 (exomes and genomes) allele frequencies

version.value: v4.1 (4.1.2 for constraint); site shows v4.1.2, v3.1.2, v2.1.1

sources.scope: 730,947 exomes and 76,215 genomes mapped to GRCh38 (v4); site-level allele counts per ancestry group, group-maximum and filtering allele frequencies, and in-silico scores carried in INFO (CADD, REVEL, SpliceAI, Pangolin, PhyloP, SIFT, PolyPhen) plus GA4GH VRS allele IDs. The header of the exome file defines 413 INFO fields and that of the genome file 240. The joint callset (exomes and genomes pooled, 664 INFO fields) carries joint, exome and genome counts side by side and the filters BOTH_FILTERED, EXOMES_FILTERED, GENOMES_FILTERED and PASS; it holds no predictor scores.
sources.mapping_methods: Coordinates on GRCh38 (v4, v3) or GRCh37 (v2.1.1 with liftover files).

quantitative.summary: Allele counts (AC), numbers (AN), frequencies (AF), homozygote counts, group-maximum (grpmax) and filtering allele frequencies (fafmax_faf95_max) per site and per ancestry group; predictor scores per allele.
quantitative.units: counts / frequency in [0, 1]; CADD phred; the other predictors on their own [0, 1] or signed scales
quantitative.uncertainty: AC/AN; filtering allele frequencies give a conservative lower bound; no confidence interval on AF
quantitative.direction: n/a (predictor scores point towards deleteriousness as defined by each tool)

licence.name: Primary exome/genome data released under CC0; some annotations carry separate terms (SpliceAI is CC BY-NC 4.0)
licence.redistribution: CC0 for primary data; honour separate annotation terms

sources.update_frequency: Major releases every few years; point releases (4.1.1, 4.1.2) in between.
coverage_limitations: An allele missing from a slice was not observed in the callset or was removed by QC; it is not a measured frequency of zero, and coverage tracks are not fetched
Case-control/cohort composition affects representativeness
Not a random sample of any population
Per-chromosome VCFs are very large (e.g. exome chr1 17.56 GiB, genome chr1 41.25 GiB)
The regional slices kept here cover only the positions of MaveDB-mapped SNVs (about 146k positions in about 1.5k regions); other regions must be sliced the same way when needed
known_omissions: Individual-level genotypes not available
Allele-frequency filtering bias against disease cohorts is noted by the consortium

reuse_decision.rationale: Whole-chromosome VCFs (11-67 GiB each) are not mirrored. The files are bgzip + tabix on a public bucket, so regions are read by HTTP range requests: slices for the genomic positions that our assets name (MaveDB-mapped SNVs) are fetched and kept; the same primitive serves later lookups for variants of interest. Absence of a record in a slice means not observed or filtered out, not a frequency of zero.

status.notes: Remote tabix over the proxy works (index opens in about 1 s; a region read takes about 0.5 s). Slices for the MaveDB positions are written by acquisition/fetch_gnomad_regional.py.

mechanism_evidence.note: SpliceAI and Pangolin scores carried in INFO

components.name: allele counts and frequencies per ancestry group
in-silico scores carried in INFO (CADD, REVEL, SpliceAI, Pangolin, PhyloP, SIFT, PolyPhen)

evidence_profile.biological_context: Aggregated germline variant calls from exome and genome sequencing cohorts, with allele counts per genetic ancestry group. No phenotype data accompany the variants.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Observed allele counts after quality filtering. Frequencies are reliable only where coverage and callability are adequate (FILTER and coverage fields) and differ by ancestry group; the in-silico scores are predictions and not measurements.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: None for mechanism. Frequency is indirect evidence: a high frequency argues against high-penetrance early-onset dominant pathogenicity, while a low frequency is consistent with pathogenicity without supporting it.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Population frequency bounds the plausible penetrance and prevalence of an allele; no phenotype is attached.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant that is not found was not observed among the sequenced individuals, whose coverage and ancestry representation are uneven. It is not evidence of rarity or harm.

sources.name: GTEx (Genotype-Tissue Expression)

version.value: v11 (946 subjects, 54 tissues, 50 eQTL tissues, GRCh38, GENCODE v47); v10 also available

sources.scope: Bulk RNA-seq expression and eQTL/sQTL resources across non-diseased tissues, plus long-read, single-cell and haplotype-expression collections in the open bucket.
sources.mapping_methods: GRCh38 genotypes with GENCODE gene annotation.

quantitative.summary: TPM, read counts, eQTL effect sizes and p-values.

licence.name: Open-access files free to download; raw sequence and full donor metadata are protected (dbGaP/AnVIL)
licence.redistribution: Open-access derivatives allowed with acknowledgement; protected data excluded
licence.note: Exact reuse wording on the documentation page was not parsed.

sources.update_frequency: Major releases every few years (v8 2019, v10, v11).
coverage_limitations: About 950 donors (946 subjects, 943 with eQTL data in release v11); donor ancestry composition is not recorded in the stored evidence and is unverified here
Sampling conditions (including post-mortem collection) are described in the GTEx publications and were not retrieved here; some tissues have few samples
Only open-access data are available here

reuse_decision.rationale: Median expression table is small and fetched now. Large eQTL tables are available but Open Targets and eQTL Catalogue provide fine-mapped, harmonised versions; pull only what is needed.

status.notes: API v2 dataset list and bucket listing verified.

unverified_fields: coverage_limitations (donor ancestry composition and sampling conditions are from the GTEx publications, not retrieved)

evidence_profile.biological_context: Bulk RNA-seq and whole-genome-sequencing genotypes from donors, across non-diseased tissues. Expression and QTL effects are averages over the cell types present in each tissue, and the number of donors differs between tissues.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Association statistics per tissue; release v11 lists 946 subjects (943 with eQTL data) in 54 tissues, 50 of them with eQTL results. Fine-mapping and colocalisation are needed before causal claims.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low to moderate. An eQTL or sQTL associates a variant, or a linked variant, with expression or splicing in a tissue; allele-specific expression collections add allele-resolved support but remain observational.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: A molecular phenotype in non-diseased tissue; disease relevance needs colocalisation with a trait and the relevant cell type or state.
evidence_profile.absence_means: No eQTL in a tissue means none was detected at the available power in bulk tissue. Cell-type-specific, context-specific and rare-allele effects are not covered.

sources.name: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog

version.value: Release files dated 2026-10-22

sources.scope: Published genome-wide association results with ontology-annotated traits, study and ancestry tables.
sources.mapping_methods: Variants mapped to Ensembl genes by distance/within-gene rules; coordinates on current assembly (GRCh38 not confirmed from the evidence retrieved).

quantitative.summary: Effect size (beta or OR), CI, p-value, risk allele frequency.

licence.name: EMBL-EBI general terms of use; summary statistics CC0 unless otherwise stated
licence.redistribution: Check per file

coverage_limitations: Lead associations rather than causal variants; ancestry bias towards European cohorts
known_omissions: Full summary statistics are in a separate repository

reuse_decision.rationale: Open Targets integrates GWAS Catalog studies into credible sets; the flat associations table is small and fetched for direct lookups. The flat studies.tsv was fetched first and discarded: it has no study accession column; the associations file carries STUDY ACCESSION.

status.notes: FTP listing verified; web REST API root URL guessed incorrectly (404) and not needed.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Published genome-wide association results with ontology-annotated traits, study and ancestry tables. Each association belongs to a study with its own cohort, ancestry, genotyping platform and imputation.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Reported association statistics (p-value, effect size and risk-allele frequency where reported). Significance thresholds apply per study, and lead variants tag a locus.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: None. An associated locus does not identify the causal variant, gene or mechanism; mapped genes are positional.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Statistical association with a trait or disease in the studied ancestry. Effects of common variants are generally small, and transfer across ancestries needs evidence.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant with no association in the catalogue has not reached the reporting threshold in catalogued studies, whose trait coverage, ancestry and power vary. It is not evidence of no effect.

sources.name: IMPC (International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium)

version.value: Data Release 24.0 (GRCm39; OpenStats 1.20.0)

sources.scope: Systematic knockout mouse phenotyping: 9,605 phenotyped genes, 10,341 mutant lines, 111,664 phenotype calls (release 24.0).
sources.mapping_methods: Mouse genes; human relevance through orthologs (Open Targets provides evidence_impc and mouse_phenotype).

quantitative.summary: Statistical significance and effect size per phenotype call.

licence.redistribution: Attribution

Homozygous knockouts mainly; hypomorphic and missense effects absent
known_omissions: Human phenotype of a human variant cannot be read directly from mouse knockouts

reuse_decision.rationale: Open Targets integrates IMPC as evidence_impc and mouse_phenotype with human ortholog mapping; fetch source tables only if gene-level mouse detail is needed.

status.notes: Release page and FTP listing readable.

mechanism_evidence.note: mouse knockout phenotype; orthology to the human gene is an inference
mouse knockout phenotype used as a proxy for loss-of-function tolerance

evidence_profile.biological_context: Knockout mouse lines phenotyped in a standardised pipeline. The genotype is an engineered knockout in one organism, and phenotype calls are made per procedure.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Direct measurement of phenotypes in knockout mice, with statistical phenotype calls and release-specific thresholds.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate for the gene's role in the mouse. It is not allele-specific, differences between mouse and human physiology limit transfer, and compensation by paralogs is not resolved.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Mouse phenotype terms. They support a human loss-of-function phenotype only when concordant with human genetics.
evidence_profile.absence_means: No phenotype call means none was detected in the procedures performed; screen breadth and genotype coverage vary, and lines that were not phenotyped or are lethal have no adult phenotype.

sources.name: InterPro

version.value: InterPro 110.0 (interpro-version response header of the API, 2026-10-25)

sources.scope: Protein families, domains and sites integrating member databases (Pfam, SMART, PROSITE, CDD, PANTHER, CATH-Gene3D and others listed by the API).

quantitative.summary: Match coordinates and signature scores.

licence.redistribution: Free, including commercial use; cite the resource and the member databases. Signature collections of included scanning tools may carry other terms.

coverage_limitations: Domain membership is predicted by signatures

status.notes: API returns JSON; per-protein matches for the MaveDB proteins are fetched by acquisition/fetch_per_protein.py.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Protein family, domain and site annotations derived from sequence signatures of member databases (Pfam, SMART, PROSITE, CDD, PANTHER, CATH-Gene3D and others).
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Signature-based computational annotation integrated from member databases. Membership is a sequence-similarity statement and not a measurement of function.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Low. It places a residue in a family, domain or site; whether a substitution there alters function needs assays, structure or conservation.

mechanism_evidence.note: deep mutational scanning and related protein assays

evidence_profile.biological_context: Each score set measures variants in a defined assay: a target sequence (gene, exon or regulatory element), an expression system, a selection or readout and a library. Scores are meaningful relative to that assay's controls and direction conventions.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Direct measurements with assay-specific replicates and, where deposited, standard errors. Scales are not harmonised across score sets, and a score set may include variants measured with few observations.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate to high for the assayed molecular function in the assayed system (for example growth, binding, abundance or reporter output). Mechanisms that give the same readout are not distinguished, and splicing or regulatory effects are missed unless the assay includes them.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: A molecular or cellular phenotype of the assay. Mapping to a disease phenotype needs calibration against clinical labels, which the repository holds only where authors supplied it.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant without a score was not measured, was filtered for low counts, or lies outside the assayed region; a position with no data is untested and not tolerant. A neutral score means no effect on the assayed function only.

sources.name: PDBe SIFTS: PDB chain to UniProt residue mappings

version.value: SIFTS flat files of 2026-10-18 (PDB release 42.26, UniProt 2026.03 per the file header); overwritten at each weekly PDB release

sources.scope: Residue-level mapping between experimentally determined PDB chains and UniProtKB sequences: mapped segments of each chain, and the segments whose residues are observed in the structure.
sources.mapping_methods: SIFTS pipeline: sequence alignment of each PDB chain to UniProtKB, giving contiguous segments in SEQRES, PDB-author and UniProt numbering.

quantitative.summary: Residue ranges of mapped and of observed segments.

licence.name: EMBL-EBI Terms of Use: freely available, no additional restriction on contributed data beyond the data owner's terms (terms page, verified live). PDB archive data files are CC0 1.0 (wwPDB usage policy, verified live). No SIFTS-specific licence statement was found.
licence.redistribution: Free with attribution; the SIFTS page asks users to cite Dana, Gutmanas et al., Nucleic Acids Research 47, D482 (2019).

coverage_limitations: Only experimentally determined structures; predicted models are in AlphaFold DB
A mapped segment says which UniProt residues a chain covers, not whether the construct carries engineered changes, nor the quality of the structure
Residue numbering differs between the SEQRES, PDB-author and UniProt systems; the UniProt columns are the ones used here
known_omissions: The other SIFTS flat files in the same directory (Pfam, InterPro, GO, CATH, SCOP, Ensembl, taxonomy, enzyme, PubMed) and the per-entry XML files are not fetched; InterPro and GO are held through InterPro and Open Targets
Coordinate files of the structures are not fetched

status.notes: Flat files listed with dates in the FTP index; the files are replaced each week, so the manifest records the size and SHA-256 of the copy fetched on 2026-10-25. pdb_chain_uniprot.tsv.gz uses CRLF line endings (a parser that splits on LF alone keeps a trailing carriage return in the last column); uniprot_segments_observed.tsv.gz uses LF.

mechanism_evidence.note: which UniProt residues are covered and observed in an experimental structure

evidence_profile.biological_context: Residue-level mapping between PDB chains and UniProtKB sequences. The structures are experimentally determined constructs, often fragments or domains with ligands or engineered changes; the mapping says which UniProt residues each chain covers and which are observed.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Experimental structures with mapping tables. Resolution and model quality belong to each structure entry and are not in the mapping.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate for the structural context of observed residues (position, burial, contacts) when the construct is relevant. It does not show the effect of a substitution, and unobserved residues have no coordinates.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None: residue mappings carry no phenotype information.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A residue not covered by any PDB chain, or not observed in the covering chains, has no experimental coordinates; this is not evidence of disorder.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Annotations linking variants, haplotypes, genes and drugs from published studies. Each annotation records the studied variant or haplotype, the drug, a phenotype category, the population and a level of evidence.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Literature-derived annotations with levels of evidence for clinical annotations. Individual studies are small and often conflict, and the annotation level is not an effect size.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Nomenclature and defining variants for star alleles of 15 pharmacogenes, on RefSeqGene, GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates. Structural variation and complex variant types are described separately from sequence haplotypes.

evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None directly.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant not in any allele definition is not a named allele, so its function is unassigned and not normal. Genes outside the 15 are not covered.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Curated tandem-repeat loci associated with Mendelian disease: locus coordinates (hg38, hg19, T2T-CHM13), repeat motif and locus structure, inheritance mode, and normal and pathogenic length thresholds.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Expert curation from the literature. Thresholds differ between loci and are summarised as single numbers; intermediate ranges, repeat interruptions and somatic instability are not captured by one threshold.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate for repeat length and motif as the disease-relevant variable at curated loci. The molecular mechanism (RNA toxicity, polyglutamine proteotoxicity, silencing) varies by locus and is not resolved by length alone.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Length above the pathogenic threshold associates with the named disease; onset, penetrance and severity depend on length and modifiers.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A locus missing from the catalogue is not curated as disease-associated. It is not shown to be benign, and the catalogue covers only loci with published disease associations.

mechanism_evidence.note: function, domain, site and modification annotations
